text:
Mara: Heads-up — customer mz-enterprise reported a sharp p99/p95 regression after we onboarded gamma-13b-micro with microtokenizer-v2 yesterday.
Mara: Symptoms: p95 from ~110ms -> ~520ms, p99 from ~430ms -> ~2.8s on long-context generation (requests that include ~20k-50k input tokens). Some requests timed out (504) in heavy tails.
Priya: Customer says this only started after model switch on 2026-03-10, they can reproduce reliably by sending long documents (legal transcripts) with lots of emoji + CJK text. They attached sample payload.
Kevin: Thanks — can you paste a minimal repro (no PII) and the exact model string used? Also how much traffic (% of their calls) hit gamma-13b-micro vs fallbacks?
Priya: Model: gamma-13b-micro@2026-03-10 (microtokenizer-v2). Traffic: 100% initially, we requested a canary but it flipped to full earlier. Repro curl they used:

curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gamma-13b-micro","input": "<~40k token legal doc + emojis>","max_output_tokens":512}'

Sanjay: I ran a run locally with their sample. Observed lots more token splitting compared to our baseline tokenizer: microtokenizer-v2 produces more subunits for emoji+CJK so sequences cross token boundaries differently. That seems to increase KV-cache misses and expand decoding steps per token for long prefixes.
Sanjay: Quick numbers from our perf logs (canary host): baseline tokenizer p99=430ms, microtokenizer-v2 p99=2.8s when input_len > 20k tokens. CPU/GPU utilization shows higher CPU time in pre-tokenizer stage and more frequent KV cache invalidation events.
Kevin: Interesting — so root cause looks like tokenization boundary shift that increases effective sequence length and K/V churn. Any sign of quantization/kernel mismatch? Or is this purely tokenization -> cache pressure?
Sanjay: Mostly tokenization -> cache pressure. No new kernel regressions. We see continuous batching sizes drop because requests land taking longer, and cache TTL gets invalidated earlier due to shifted prefixes. Also some RPC timeouts between runtime and tokenizer microservice under tail load.
Tess: Oncall action list: 1) throttle customer to prevent cascade, 2) route them to fallback model gamma-13b-base (older tokenizer) while we triage, 3) rollback tokenizer flag for model if quick rollback available.
Mara: Customer wants a mitigation ASAP. Priya, can we flip a routing rule to force their org to gamma-13b-base for now? Kevin, can engineering drop a short rollback if it's config-only?
Priya: I can create a temporary override in the routing rules to pin their org to gamma-13b-base. Will do 5-mineta and report.
Kevin: Engineering: there is a config flag in model catalog to disable microtokenizer-v2 for specific model revisions. We can set model_config.gamma-13b-micro.tokenizer=legacy for that org in under 15 mins. I'll prepare the PR and a hotpatch.
Sanjay: For longer-term: we should add a tokenization diff check in the onboarding pipeline — compute token count deltas for representative corpora and flag > 5% increase in effective tokens for longctx workloads.
Sanjay: Also propose: 1) enable prefix-only caching for sequences > 10k tokens (don't cache intermediate KV across user-provided boundaries), 2) increase tokenizer microservice CPU limit and add async pre-tokenization for large inputs.
Tess: Immediate mitigation steps I executed: - throttled mz-enterprise to 30rps - applied routing override to gamma-13b-base for org mz-enterprise - set alert mute while we stabilize (ops-override)
deploy-bot: canary-deploy/gamma-13b-micro-2026-03-10: rollback requested by Kevin. Status: in-progress.
Kevin: Rolling back tokenizer flag globally is risky; prefer targeted override for the affected orgs/customers. We'll roll forward a targeted config change first. If we see system-wide adoption issues, we'll consider global rollback.
Priya: Confirmed customer is back on gamma-13b-base and their p99 dropped back near baseline within 10 minutes. They're able to proceed.
Mara: Next steps: Sanjay to scope tokenizer diff check task and PR for onboarding gate. Kevin to land targeted model_config override hotpatch. Priya to monitor customer for 24 hours. Tess to keep incident notes.
Sanjay: I'll open a ticket in eng-ml with perf diffs and proposed onboarding check (include CJK/emoji-heavy corpora). Will also add a small test harness to simulate 30k+ token docs.
Kevin: Also adding a lightweight dashboard: per-model tokenizer delta (tokens/input char ratio) and longctx p95/p99 trend — helps catch regressions early.
Mara: Thanks team. Log summary for incident notes:
- Root cause: microtokenizer-v2 increased subtokenization for mixed-language + emoji inputs -> longer effective sequences -> KV cache churn and tokenizer microservice CPU/RPC tail latency -> p95/p99 spikes on long-context requests.
- Immediate mitigation: org-level routing override to older tokenizer/model; throttle; targeted config hotpatch in model catalog.
- Long-term: onboarding gating (token delta), prefix-caching change, tokenizer microservice autoscale and async path.
Tess: I'll file the postmortem template and mark severity as P2 since customer impact isolated and mitigated.
Mara: Closing thread once tickets are up and monitoring shows stable tails. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
